drugs.mechanism: Selective estrogen receptor modulator; tamoxifen and particularly its active metabolites antagonize ER-mediated transcription in breast tissue.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for breast cancer treatment and specified risk-reduction indications.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensively tested in randomized breast cancer trials as an ER-directed endocrine therapy.

drugs.mechanism: Active tamoxifen metabolite that binds and antagonizes estrogen receptor-alpha.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not separately FDA-approved as a drug.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Studied as an investigational ER-directed drug in Phase 1 and Phase 2 breast cancer trials.

drugs.mechanism: Active tamoxifen metabolite that binds estrogen receptor-alpha and modulates its transcriptional activity.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not separately FDA-approved as a drug.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Topical formulations have been studied in Phase 2 trials in ER-positive ductal carcinoma in situ.

drugs.mechanism: Selective estrogen receptor modulator with antiestrogenic activity in breast tissue.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for metastatic breast cancer in postmenopausal women with ER-positive or ER-unknown tumors.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Tested in randomized breast cancer trials as an ER-directed endocrine therapy.

drugs.mechanism: Binds ER, antagonizes its activity, and promotes receptor degradation.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified HR-positive advanced breast cancer settings, alone or in combinations.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensively tested in Phase 3 ER-directed breast cancer trials, including endocrine and targeted-therapy combinations.

drugs.mechanism: Oral selective estrogen receptor antagonist and degrader.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified previously treated ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 EMERALD evaluated ER-directed treatment in advanced breast cancer, including the ESR1-mutated population.

drugs.mechanism: Oral selective estrogen receptor antagonist and degrader.
drugs.fdaStatus: The review reports FDA approval in September 2025 for specified previously treated ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 EMBER-3 evaluated ER-directed treatment in advanced breast cancer, including ESR1-mutated disease.

drugs.mechanism: ER-binding PROTAC that recruits a cereblon-containing E3 ligase to promote ER ubiquitination and degradation; a purpose-developed oncology agent, not a repurposed nononcology drug.
drugs.fdaStatus: Presented as investigational in the review; the supplied preclinical study does not establish FDA approval.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Studied clinically for ER degradation, including the Phase 3 VERITAC-2 trial in ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Purpose-developed oral ER antagonist and degrader.
drugs.fdaStatus: Presented as investigational in the review; no FDA approval is established by the supplied text.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Studied in Phase 2 and Phase 3 ER-directed breast cancer trials, including SERENA-2 and SERENA-6.

drugs.mechanism: Purpose-developed oral ER antagonist and degrader.
drugs.fdaStatus: Presented as investigational in the review; no FDA approval is established by the supplied text.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Studied in Phase 2 and Phase 3 ER-directed breast cancer trials, including acelERA and persevERA.

drugs.mechanism: Synthetic progestin and progesterone receptor agonist with complex endocrine antitumor effects.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for palliative treatment of advanced breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Tested in clinical breast cancer endocrine-therapy trials; these do not establish selective inhibition of oncogenic PGR signaling.

drugs.mechanism: Progesterone receptor antagonist; also antagonizes the glucocorticoid receptor, which is outside the requested target list.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for non-breast-cancer indications; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: PR-directed clinical studies have been conducted in breast cancer, including early-phase and presurgical studies.
Studied in early-phase PR-directed trials in breast cancer and other hormone-dependent malignancies.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding HER2 extracellular domain IV; produces receptor-related effects and immune-mediated cytotoxicity.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified HER2-positive breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensively tested in Phase 3 HER2-directed breast cancer trials in early and metastatic disease.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding HER2 extracellular domain II and inhibiting HER2 heterodimerization.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in combinations for specified HER2-positive breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials including CLEOPATRA and APHINITY evaluated HER2-directed treatment.

drugs.mechanism: Fc-engineered anti-HER2 antibody designed to enhance immune effector activity.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with chemotherapy for specified previously treated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 SOPHIA evaluated HER2-directed treatment in previously treated metastatic breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Reversible ATP-site inhibitor of HER2 and EGFR; EGFR is outside the requested target list.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in specified combinations for HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Tested in Phase 3 HER2-directed breast cancer trials, including combinations with capecitabine or endocrine therapy.

drugs.mechanism: Irreversible covalent inhibitor of HER2, EGFR, and HER4; only HER2 is in the requested target list.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified extended-adjuvant and metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 ExteNET and NALA evaluated HER2-directed treatment.

drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with trastuzumab and capecitabine for specified previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer, including eligible patients with brain metastases.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: The randomized HER2CLIMB trial evaluated HER2 inhibition in metastatic breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases.

drugs.mechanism: Fluoropyrimidine prodrug converted to fluorouracil; metabolites inhibit thymidylate synthase and disrupt nucleic acids. No listed protein is its established direct therapeutic target.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for breast cancer and other malignancies.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; extensively tested in breast cancer as chemotherapy, including HER2-directed combinations.

drugs.mechanism: The antibody binds HER2 and delivers DM1, which inhibits microtubules. Neither its payload nor its principal cytotoxic mechanism targets TOP1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified HER2-positive early and metastatic breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 EMILIA and KATHERINE evaluated HER2-directed ADC delivery.

drugs.mechanism: Maytansinoid payload that binds tubulin and disrupts microtubules; tubulin is outside the requested target list.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not separately FDA-approved as a standalone drug; an approved ADC payload in T-DM1.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; clinically tested as the microtubule-directed payload of T-DM1, not as a HER2- or TOP1-binding drug.

drugs.mechanism: The antibody binds HER2; released DXd payload stabilizes TOP1-DNA cleavage complexes. HER2 targeting and TOP1 poisoning occur through different ADC components.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified HER2-positive, HER2-low, and selected HR-positive HER2-ultralow breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 DESTINY-Breast trials evaluated HER2-directed delivery of a TOP1-inhibitory payload, including HER2-low and ultralow populations.

drugs.mechanism: TOP1 poison that stabilizes TOP1-DNA cleavage complexes; does not itself bind HER2 or TROP2 for delivery.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not separately FDA-approved as a standalone drug; used as a payload in approved ADCs.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinically tested as a TOP1-inhibitory ADC payload in the DESTINY-Breast and TROPION-Breast programs; this is not evidence of approval as free DXd.

drugs.mechanism: Selective inhibition of the PI3K p110-alpha catalytic subunit.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with fulvestrant for specified PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 SOLAR-1 evaluated PI3K-alpha inhibition in PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor that also promotes degradation of mutant p110-alpha.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in October 2024 with palbociclib and fulvestrant for specified endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 INAVO120 evaluated PI3K-alpha targeting with palbociclib and fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-competitive pan-AKT inhibitor targeting AKT1, AKT2, and AKT3. PIK3CA and PTEN alterations are selection biomarkers, not additional direct binding targets.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with fulvestrant for specified HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with qualifying PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN alterations.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 CAPItello-291 evaluated AKT inhibition in advanced breast cancer, including tumors with qualifying pathway alterations.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-competitive pan-AKT inhibitor; does not directly restore or inhibit PTEN.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 LOTUS and Phase 3 IPATunity170/IPATunity130 studied AKT inhibition in breast cancer; an established clinical benefit was not demonstrated across these settings.

drugs.mechanism: Binds FKBP12; the resulting complex engages mTOR and predominantly allosterically inhibits mTORC1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with exemestane for specified previously treated advanced HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 BOLERO-2 evaluated mTOR inhibition with exemestane in advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-competitive catalytic mTOR inhibitor targeting both mTORC1 and mTORC2.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Studied in early-phase and Phase 2 trials of mTOR inhibition, including endocrine-therapy combinations in advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-competitive catalytic inhibitor of mTORC1 and mTORC2.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 MANTA evaluated mTOR inhibition with fulvestrant in ER-positive advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Antidiabetic drug affecting mitochondrial energetics and systemic insulin signaling, with possible AMPK-associated suppression of mTORC1; not an established direct mTOR binder.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials establishing direct binding to the listed targets. Phase 3 MA.32 tested breast cancer repurposing, not direct mTOR inhibition, and did not establish broad benefit in patients without diabetes.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-site CDK4/6 inhibitor that indirectly reduces RB phosphorylation; does not directly bind RB1 or inhibit cyclin D.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in specified combinations for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 PALOMA trials evaluated CDK4/6 inhibition in advanced breast cancer; INAVO120 evaluated its combination with inavolisib and fulvestrant.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-site CDK4/6 inhibitor that reduces RB phosphorylation indirectly.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified advanced breast cancer regimens and with an aromatase inhibitor for selected high-risk stage II-III early breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 MONALEESA trials and the adjuvant NATALEE trial evaluated CDK4/6 inhibition.

drugs.mechanism: ATP-site CDK4/6 inhibitor that indirectly maintains growth-suppressive hypophosphorylated RB.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified advanced breast cancer settings and with endocrine therapy for selected high-risk, node-positive early breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 MONARCH, monarchE, and postMONARCH trials evaluated CDK4/6 inhibition, including adjuvant treatment and treatment after prior CDK4/6 inhibition.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding PD-1 and blocking its interactions with PD-L1 and PD-L2; does not directly bind PD-L1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified high-risk early TNBC and PD-L1 CPS ≥10 unresectable or metastatic TNBC regimens; additional tumor-agnostic indications may apply.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 KEYNOTE-522 and KEYNOTE-355 evaluated PD-1 blockade in early and advanced TNBC.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody directly binding PD-L1 to block inhibitory immune signaling.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for other malignancies; its former US breast cancer indication with nab-paclitaxel was withdrawn.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 IMpassion130 and IMpassion131 evaluated PD-L1 blockade in advanced TNBC; trial testing does not imply a current US breast cancer indication.

drugs.mechanism: Albumin-bound paclitaxel that binds tubulin and stabilizes microtubules; none of the requested proteins is its established direct target.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for breast cancer and other malignancies; the atezolizumab breast cancer combination indication was withdrawn.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets as direct nab-paclitaxel targets; tested as chemotherapy alongside PD-L1 blockade in IMpassion130.

drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PARP1/2 catalytic activity and traps PARP-DNA complexes. Exploits BRCA-associated repair deficiency without directly binding BRCA1 or BRCA2 as therapeutic targets.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic and high-risk early breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 OlympiAD and OlympiA evaluated PARP inhibition in germline BRCA-mutated breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 catalytic inhibitor with potent PARP trapping; BRCA1/2 deficiency is a sensitivity context rather than a direct binding target.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 EMBRACA evaluated PARP inhibition in germline BRCA-mutated advanced breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Kinase inhibitor targeting mutant BRAF, including BRAF V600E; does not directly inhibit RAS, MEK, or ERK.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with trametinib for qualifying BRAF V600E-mutated solid tumors under a tumor-agnostic indication, as well as other specified indications; not a general breast cancer approval.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: BRAF V600E-directed trials include the Phase 2 ROAR and NCI-MATCH basket programs with trametinib; breast cancer applicability is molecularly selected.

drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with dabrafenib for qualifying BRAF V600E-mutated solid tumors under a tumor-agnostic indication and for other specified indications; not a general breast cancer approval.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: MEK inhibition has been tested in Phase 3 melanoma trials and Phase 2 BRAF-selected basket trials with dabrafenib, as well as investigational breast cancer combinations.

drugs.mechanism: Covalently binds KRAS G12C in its GDP-bound state; not a pan-RAS inhibitor.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified KRAS G12C-mutated non-breast cancers; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: KRAS G12C inhibition has been tested in the CodeBreaK clinical program, including Phase 2 and Phase 3 NSCLC trials and colorectal cancer trials.

drugs.mechanism: Covalent inhibitor of GDP-bound KRAS G12C; not a pan-RAS inhibitor.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified KRAS G12C-mutated non-breast cancers; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: KRAS G12C inhibition has been tested in the KRYSTAL clinical program, including NSCLC and colorectal cancer trials.

drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified neurofibromatosis type 1-associated plexiform neurofibromas; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: MEK inhibition has been tested in NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma trials and in breast cancer studies, including a randomized Phase 2 fulvestrant combination trial.

drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved with encorafenib for specified BRAF-mutated non-breast cancers; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: MEK inhibition has been tested in Phase 3 BRAF-mutated melanoma trials and early-phase breast cancer combination studies.
Studied in Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials targeting ERK signaling in advanced solid tumors, including molecularly selected MAPK-altered tumors.
Studied in Phase 1 trials of ERK inhibition in advanced solid tumors.

drugs.mechanism: Nonsteroidal reversible aromatase inhibitor interacting with the heme-containing catalytic site of CYP19A1; does not directly target ESR1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified postmenopausal HR-positive breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensively tested in randomized aromatase-inhibition trials, including Phase 3 ATAC.

drugs.mechanism: Nonsteroidal reversible inhibitor of CYP19A1 that reduces estrogen synthesis.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified postmenopausal HR-positive breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensively tested in Phase 3 aromatase-inhibition trials, including BIG 1-98 and MA.17.

drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified postmenopausal HR-positive breast cancer settings, including use with everolimus under the combination indication.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Tested in randomized aromatase-inhibition trials, including the Intergroup Exemestane Study and endocrine combinations such as BOLERO-2.

drugs.mechanism: The antibody binds TROP2, which is outside the requested target list, and delivers SN-38, which poisons TOP1. The antibody itself does not bind TOP1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified previously treated unresectable or metastatic TNBC and HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer settings.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 ASCENT and TROPiCS-02 evaluated TROP2-directed delivery of a TOP1-inhibitory payload in breast cancer.

drugs.mechanism: Active irinotecan metabolite and sacituzumab govitecan payload that stabilizes TOP1-DNA cleavage complexes.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not separately FDA-approved as a standalone drug; delivered by approved irinotecan products and sacituzumab govitecan.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: TOP1-directed clinical exposure occurs through irinotecan and investigational delivery formulations, and through the Phase 3 sacituzumab govitecan breast cancer programs.

drugs.mechanism: The antibody binds TROP2, outside the requested target list, and delivers a deruxtecan TOP1-inhibitory payload. TOP1 engagement is mediated by released payload.
drugs.fdaStatus: The review reports FDA approval in January 2025 for eligible previously treated HR-positive, HER2-negative unresectable or metastatic breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 TROPION-Breast01 evaluated TROP2-directed delivery of a TOP1-inhibitory payload.

drugs.mechanism: Prodrug converted to SN-38, the principal active TOP1 poison; TOP1 engagement is predominantly metabolite-mediated.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for colorectal cancer regimens; no established breast cancer indication.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: TOP1-directed treatment has been extensively tested in colorectal cancer and in Phase 2 breast cancer trials.

drugs.mechanism: TOP1 poison stabilizing TOP1-DNA cleavage complexes and preventing efficient DNA religation.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for specified ovarian, small-cell lung, and cervical cancer settings; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: TOP1-directed treatment has been tested in trials supporting its non-breast indications and in Phase 2 advanced breast cancer studies.

drugs.mechanism: Anthelmintic with reported mitochondrial uncoupling and indirect modulation of signaling, including mTOR-associated pathways; the review does not establish direct binding to any requested protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: Has FDA approval history as an anthelmintic; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets as established direct niclosamide targets; early oncology repurposing studies do not demonstrate selective direct mTOR inhibition.

drugs.mechanism: Natural product discussed through a diabetic kidney disease study; the supplied evidence does not establish a therapeutically relevant direct interaction with any requested protein in breast cancer.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not FDA-approved as a breast cancer treatment or as an anticancer drug.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets establishing the direct interactions proposed in this review; exploratory human studies do not establish target-specific breast cancer efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Unspecified natural-product candidate discussed in a gastric-protection study; pathway modulation does not establish direct binding to any requested protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: No FDA approval for an identifiable breast cancer drug is established by the supplied text.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; the specific flavonoid is not identified.

drugs.mechanism: Natural-product candidate discussed through cervical cancer findings; no validated direct interaction with the requested proteins is established in the supplied text.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not FDA-approved as a breast cancer treatment.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets.

drugs.mechanism: Named only within the FKBP12-rapamycin-binding domain terminology in the review. Pharmacologically, its FKBP12 complex allosterically inhibits mTORC1.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for non-breast-cancer indications, including transplant immunosuppression and lymphangioleiomyomatosis; not approved for breast cancer.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: mTOR inhibition has been studied in early-phase oncology trials, including breast cancer combinations; the supplied text does not discuss these trials.
